unit.label: Sports, music & choices
unit.title: Sports, Music & Choices
unit.description: 6 new words and expressions. Talk about music and sports, ask someone to choose, and explain your preferences.

goal.text: 你喜歡打籃球還是踢足球？
goal.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuān dǎ lánqiú háishì tī zúqiú?
goal.meaning: Do you like playing basketball or soccer?

unit.bookReference: A Course in Contemporary Chinese 1 · Lesson 3 週末做什麼？ · vocabulary pp. 46, 48; topic sentences pp. 52–53; frequency pp. 54–55; choice practice p. 59

lessons.title: Listen to Music
lessons.subtitle: Add music to the activities you enjoy

steps.prompt: In 我喜歡游泳, what does 喜歡 tell you?
steps.explanation: 喜歡 says what someone likes.

steps.prompt: Which activity means “listen to music”?
steps.explanation: 聽 is listen and 音樂 is music.
In 音樂, 樂 is read yuè. The full word is yīnyuè.
steps.prompt: Listen to the word for music. Which character is its second syllable?
In 音樂 (yīnyuè), how do you read 樂?
steps.explanation: This word uses yuè. A character can have a different reading in a different word.

steps.prompt: Which word places an activity tomorrow?
steps.explanation: 明天 means tomorrow.

steps.prompt: A friend says 我不常運動. What can you conclude?
steps.explanation: 不常 tells you how often. Disliking it would require 不喜歡.
Listen for 運動, yùndòng. 動 is its fourth-tone second syllable.
steps.prompt: Listen to the word for exercise. Which character is its second syllable?
Which component sits on the right of 動?
steps.explanation: 動 has the nine-stroke 重 on the left and the two-stroke 力 on the right.

lessons.title: Play Basketball
lessons.subtitle: Learn the sport together with its verb

steps.prompt: In 我們一起游泳, what does 一起 add?
steps.explanation: 一起 makes the activity shared.
Listen for 籃球, lánqiú. 籃 is the second-tone first syllable.
steps.prompt: Listen to the word for basketball. Which character is its first syllable?
Which part of 打籃球 names the sport?
steps.explanation: 籃球 is basketball; 打 is the action word.

lessons.title: Play Soccer
lessons.subtitle: Choose the action word that fits the sport

steps.prompt: Which phrase introduces your opinion?
steps.explanation: 覺得 introduces what you think or feel.

steps.prompt: Which activity uses the verb 踢?
steps.explanation: 踢 means kick, which fits soccer.
踢 is tī, a high level first tone; 足球 is zúqiú.
steps.prompt: Listen to the expression for playing soccer. Which character is the action verb?
Which component gives the useful foot clue in 踢?
steps.explanation: The left 足 component is the foot clue. The right-hand component is 易.

lessons.title: Which Activity Would You Choose?
lessons.subtitle: Add tennis and ask a real choice question

steps.prompt: A friend suggests a plan. Which response accepts warmly?
steps.explanation: 好啊 is a warm acceptance.

steps.prompt: 你想打網球還是游泳？ Which answer clearly chooses swimming?
steps.explanation: The question asks which activity. Naming 游泳 makes the choice clear.

steps.prompt: What does 還是 ask the listener to do here?
steps.explanation: 還是 joins the alternatives in a choice question.
In 還是, 還 is hái. Listen to the whole word háishì.
steps.prompt: Listen to the word for or in a choice question. Which character is its first syllable?

lessons.title: Tell Us Your Preferences
lessons.subtitle: Make an activity the topic; say you like both

steps.prompt: In 我們都喜歡游泳, who likes swimming?
steps.explanation: The familiar 都 includes all members of 我們.

steps.prompt: In 打網球，我喜歡, what is the topic?
steps.explanation: 打網球 is placed first to name what the comment is about.

steps.prompt: In 打籃球、踢足球，我都喜歡, what does 都 include?
steps.explanation: The topic lists two activities; 我都喜歡 says I like both of them.

steps.prompt: A: 你喜歡打籃球還是踢足球？ B: 打籃球、踢足球，我都喜歡。 What does B prefer?
steps.explanation: B uses the two activities as the topic and 都喜歡 as the comment.

steps.prompt: A friend says 我喜歡打網球。我不常打網球。 Is this a contradiction?
options: No: liking and frequency are different
Yes: liking means doing it often
steps.answer: No: liking and frequency are different
steps.explanation: A person can enjoy tennis and still not play it often. 不常 does not mean never.

steps.prompt: A: 你明天想打網球還是游泳？ B: 我想游泳。 A: 好啊！ Which activity did they agree on?
steps.explanation: B names swimming; A accepts that choice with 好啊.

lessons.title: Sports, Music & Choices — Review
lessons.subtitle: Use the words, characters and choices together

steps.prompt: Which familiar expression asks how a proposed plan sounds?
steps.explanation: After a proposal, 怎麼樣 asks for the other person’s reaction.
網球 is wǎngqiú, tennis. 網 has the third-tone syllable wǎng.
steps.prompt: Listen to the word for tennis. Which character is its first syllable?
你想打網球還是游泳？ Which answer explicitly chooses tennis?
steps.explanation: A choice question needs the chosen activity to be clear.

steps.prompt: Which sentence means “I also exercise often”?
steps.explanation: 也常 means also often. Adding 不 would change the meaning to also not often; 不喜歡 describes a dislike.

steps.prompt: A: 你喜歡聽音樂還是看電影？ B: 聽音樂、看電影，我都喜歡。 What does B say?
steps.explanation: B uses the topic pattern and 都 to include both activities.

newVocabulary.note: Use the familiar 聽: 聽音樂, listen to music. In this word 樂 is yuè.
Use 運動 as an activity by itself; it does not need a following object.
打 means hit/play here; 籃球 is basketball. Learn the sport with its verb.
踢 means kick; 足球 is soccer, also called football.
網球 is tennis; 網 means net. This sport also uses 打.
Put 還是 between the alternatives. Do not add 嗎 to this choice-question pattern.

音.note: 音 is the first character of 音樂 (yīnyuè), music. It has 立 above 日. Keep the lower box narrower than the long horizontal above it.
音.memory: For 音, place the five-stroke 立 over a four-stroke 日. The top and bottom share one vertical centre.

parts.label: 立
parts.name: upper standing shape
parts.description: Write the dot, horizontal, two inward strokes, and long horizontal of 立 before the lower box.

parts.label: 日
parts.name: lower sun-shaped box
parts.description: Under 立, write the upright 日 box with one horizontal line inside. This is a visible shape cue.

樂.note: In 音樂 (yīnyuè), 樂 is pronounced yuè. The Taiwan stroke sequence starts with the central 白, then the two small 幺 groups, and finishes with 木 below.
樂.memory: Find the central 白, one curled 幺 on each side, and a wide 木 base. Three upper groups balance over the lower wood shape.

parts.label: 白
parts.name: central white-shaped box
parts.description: Begin with the five strokes of 白 in the upper centre; do not begin with the far-left curl.

parts.label: 幺
parts.name: left curled group
parts.description: Three compact strokes curl down the left of 白. Leave space between the curl and the centre.

parts.label: 幺
parts.name: right curled group
parts.description: Write the matching three-stroke curl to the right of 白 after completing the left one.

parts.label: 木
parts.name: wood base
parts.description: Finish with four strokes below: a horizontal, central vertical, and two spreading lower strokes.

樂.partOrderLabel: central 白, left 幺, right 幺, then 木

運.note: 運 begins 運動 (yùndòng), to exercise. Write the inner 軍 first, then the four-stroke Taiwan movement component 辶 around its left and bottom.
運.memory: 運 has a covered 車 inside 軍, resting above the long sweeping path of 辶. Finish the outside path last.

parts.label: 軍
parts.name: inner covered vehicle shape
parts.description: The nine inner strokes form 軍: a two-stroke cover above 車. Keep the inner group high enough for the path below.

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: movement surround
parts.description: Four strokes form the Taiwan movement component. Its final long sweep supports the entire inner 軍.

運.partOrderLabel: inside 軍 first, then the surrounding 辶

動.meaning: move; second syllable of 運動
動.note: 動 is the second character of 運動 (yùndòng). The left component is 重; the two strokes of 力 sit on the right.
動.memory: Keep the layered 重 tall and compact, then add the hooked 力 and its slant on the right.

parts.label: 重
parts.name: layered left component
parts.description: The nine strokes of 重 include a central vertical and stacked horizontal lines. Finish this entire left component first.

parts.label: 力
parts.name: strength component
parts.description: A bent hook and a falling leftward stroke form 力 on the right. The hook leaves room for the final slant.

打.note: 打 is used in 打籃球, play basketball. Learn each sport with its own action verb.
打.memory: 打 is 扌 + 丁: the narrow hand component stands beside a horizontal bar with a vertical hook.

parts.label: 扌
parts.name: hand component
parts.description: 扌 forms the three strokes on the left. The hand component suits an activity done with the hands.

parts.label: 丁
parts.name: right-hand bar and hook
parts.description: 丁 has just two strokes: a horizontal above a vertical hook. Keep that simple right side open.

籃.note: 籃球 (lánqiú) means basketball. 籃 has the bamboo component 竹 at the top and 監 below. At the bottom of 監, a wide 皿 forms a stable base.
籃.memory: 籃 has the bamboo component 竹 at the top and 監 below. At the bottom of 監, a wide 皿 forms a stable base.

parts.label: 竹
parts.name: 竹 component
parts.description: The six top strokes form the compact bamboo component. Its two small groups sit side by side above the larger lower part.

parts.label: 監
parts.name: 監 component
parts.description: The fourteen strokes below the bamboo form 監. Notice its upper clusters above the long, shallow 皿 at the bottom.

球.note: 足球 (zúqiú) means soccer; football. 球 is 王 beside 求. The left jade component is narrow; 求 spreads out around a central hooked vertical on the right.
球.memory: 球 is 王 beside 求. The left jade component is narrow; 求 spreads out around a central hooked vertical on the right.

parts.label: 王
parts.name: 王 component
parts.description: The four-stroke jade component looks like a narrow 王. Its final stroke rises toward the right in this side form.

parts.label: 求
parts.name: 求 component
parts.description: 求 includes a central hooked stroke and spreading marks on both sides. Remember the small dot near its upper right.

踢.note: 踢足球 (tī zúqiú) means play soccer; football. 踢 places the foot component 足 beside 易. The foot is a useful clue for kicking; 易 has 日 above two slants inside a hooked outline.
踢.memory: 踢 places the foot component 足 beside 易. The foot is a useful clue for kicking; 易 has 日 above two slants inside a hooked outline.

parts.label: 足
parts.name: 足 component
parts.description: The left foot component begins with 口, then narrows beneath it. Its final rising stroke makes room for the right side.

parts.label: 易
parts.name: 易 component
parts.description: The eight strokes on the right make 易: 日 above a hooked lower group with two inner slants.

足.note: 足 means foot. It begins 足球, soccer/football, the sport played by kicking the ball.
足.memory: 足 has 口 above a lower group that stretches down and then across to the right, like a planted foot.

parts.label: 口
parts.name: upper mouth-shaped box
parts.description: The first three strokes form a small 口 at the top of 足. This is a shape cue, not a literal explanation of the meaning.

parts.label: lower
parts.name: lower leg and foot shape
parts.description: Below 口, a central vertical and short bar lead into two spreading strokes. The final stroke makes a long base to the right.

網.note: 網球 (wǎngqiú) means tennis. 網 has the thread component 糹 on the left and 罔 on the right; the thread shape is a useful memory cue for a net.
網.memory: A narrow 糹 stands beside the wider frame of 罔. Keep the three final dots of 糹 distinct before moving to the right side.

parts.label: 糹
parts.name: thread component
parts.description: Six strokes make the narrow thread component, including three small finishing dots. Complete all six before the right frame.

parts.label: 罔
parts.name: right framed component
parts.description: Eight strokes form 罔. Start with the outer left and hooked top-right frame, then write the small shapes inside it.

還.note: 還是 (háishì) means or (in a choice question). 還 places 睘 inside the movement component 辶. Look for the wide net-shaped top inside, and the long path sweeping underneath.
還.memory: 還 places 睘 inside the movement component 辶. Look for the wide net-shaped top inside, and the long path sweeping underneath.

parts.label: 睘
parts.name: 睘 component
parts.description: The thirteen inner strokes form 睘, beginning with a wide net-shaped box. Keep the smaller shapes below it centered.

parts.label: 辶
parts.name: 辶 component
parts.description: Write the four-stroke Taiwan movement component last, down the left and across the base. In 還是, read 還 as hái, not huán.

還.partOrderLabel: inside first, then the surrounding movement component

u9-music.title: Listen to music
u9-music.explanation: 音樂 (yīnyuè) means music. You already know 聽, to listen: 聽音樂 means listen to music, with no extra word for English “to.” Put 喜歡 before the whole activity to say you like it. 樂 has more than one reading; in 音樂 use yuè. Learn the two characters together as this word.

examples.meaning: Do you like listening to music?

u9-music.remember: 音樂 is the thing you listen to; 聽音樂 is the activity.

u9-exercise.title: Exercise is an activity
u9-exercise.explanation: 運動 (yùndòng) means to exercise. The complete word can be the action: 我運動, I exercise. Add the familiar 常 for often, or 想 for wanting to do it. You do not need to add 做 before 運動 in these sentences. 運 and 動 work together as one activity word.
u9-exercise.remember: 常運動 describes a habit; 想運動 describes a wish.

u9-frequency.title: Often, also often, or not often
u9-frequency.explanation: You know 常, often. 不常 means not often: put 不 before 常. It describes frequency, not whether you enjoy the activity. 我不常運動 does not tell us whether I like exercise. When adding “also,” put 也 first: 也常, also often, or 也不常, also not often. These words all come before the action.

examples.text: 她常聽音樂，我也常聽音樂。
examples.pinyin: Tā cháng tīng yīnyuè, wǒ yě cháng tīng yīnyuè.
examples.meaning: She often listens to music; I also often listen to music.

examples.text: 他不常運動，我也不常運動。
examples.pinyin: Tā bù cháng yùndòng, wǒ yě bù cháng yùndòng.
examples.meaning: He does not exercise often; I do not exercise often either.

u9-frequency.remember: 不常 = not often. 不喜歡 = do not like. Put 也 before 不 and 常.

u9-basketball.title: Play basketball
u9-basketball.explanation: 打籃球 (dǎ lánqiú) means play basketball. 打 means hit or play in this expression; 籃球 (lánqiú) is basketball. 籃 means basket and 球 means ball. Chinese does not use one action word for every sport, so learn each sport together with its verb. Reuse 喜歡 + activity to describe a preference, and 去 + activity to go and do it.

examples.meaning: We are going to play basketball tomorrow.

u9-basketball.remember: Keep the pair 打籃球: play + basketball. 籃 contains the bamboo top; 球 is the ball.

u9-soccer.title: Kick the ball: play soccer
u9-soccer.explanation: 踢足球 (tī zúqiú) means play soccer, or football. 踢 means kick; 足球 (zúqiú) names the sport. 足 means foot, while 球 is the ball you learned in 籃球. Use 踢 for soccer and 打 for basketball. To say you like playing, put 喜歡 before 踢足球. To suggest going to play, reuse 我們 + 去 + activity + 吧.
u9-soccer.remember: 打籃球 uses 打; 踢足球 uses 踢. The foot component in 踢 helps you remember kicking.

u9-tennis.title: One more sport: tennis
u9-tennis.explanation: 打網球 (dǎ wǎngqiú) means play tennis. 網球 (wǎngqiú) is tennis; 網 means net and 球 is the familiar ball character. Like basketball, tennis uses 打. Only 網 is a new character in this sport: reuse 打 and 球.
u9-tennis.remember: 打籃球 = play basketball; 打網球 = play tennis; 踢足球 = play soccer.

u9-choice.title: Ask someone to choose
u9-choice.pattern: 你 + 想 / 喜歡 + activity A + 還是 + activity B？
u9-choice.explanation: 還是 (háishì) means “or” in a question offering alternatives. Put it between the two activities. The shared 你想 or 你喜歡 applies to both choices. 你想打網球還是游泳？ asks which you want to do, not simply yes or no. Name the activity in your answer. For this direct choice-question pattern, do not add 嗎. If both appeal, you can say 我喜歡…，也喜歡… using the familiar 也.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng dǎ wǎngqiú háishì yóuyǒng?
examples.meaning: Do you want to play tennis or swim?

examples.text: 你喜歡聽音樂還是看電影？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuān tīng yīnyuè háishì kàn diànyǐng?
examples.meaning: Do you like listening to music or watching movies?

u9-choice.remember: 還是 offers choices. 嗎 asks yes or no. Answer a choice question by naming your choice.

u9-topic.title: Put the activity you are discussing first
u9-topic.explanation: You can begin by naming the activity you want to discuss, then say what you think about it. This first part is the topic. 我喜歡打網球 becomes 打網球，我喜歡: “As for playing tennis, I like it.” The person 我 still comes before 喜歡 in the comment. Do not add 是, 的, or a second object for English “it.” Starting with the activity makes clear what your comment is about.

examples.meaning: As for playing tennis, I like it.
As for listening to music, I like it a lot.

u9-topic.remember: Name the topic first; then say who feels or does what. The order exercises here start with the activity.

u9-both-topics.title: Talk about both activities
u9-both-topics.pattern: activity A、activity B，person + 都 + 喜歡
u9-both-topics.explanation: When you name two activities as the topic and say you like both, use 都 in the comment. Its meaning now points back to the two activities at the beginning. 打籃球、踢足球，我都喜歡 means I like both playing basketball and playing soccer. Keep 都 after 我 and before 喜歡. This lets you answer a choice question by saying both appeal to you.

examples.text: 打籃球、踢足球，我都喜歡。
examples.pinyin: Dǎ lánqiú, tī zúqiú, wǒ dōu xǐhuān.
examples.meaning: As for playing basketball and soccer, I like both.

u9-both-topics.remember: Two activities first; then 我都喜歡. Here 都 includes both activities, not a group of people.

u9-music-like.note: Keep 聽 and 音樂 together as the activity.

u9-music-question.meaning: Do you like listening to music?
u9-music-question.note: The familiar 嗎 turns the statement into a yes/no question.

u9-exercise-often.note: 運動 is the whole action.

u9-music-also-often.meaning: I also often listen to music.

u9-exercise-also-not-often.meaning: I do not exercise often either.
u9-exercise-also-not-often.note: Use the order 也, 不, 常, then the activity.

u9-basketball-like.note: 喜歡 comes before the complete activity 打籃球.

u9-basketball-tomorrow.meaning: We are going to play basketball tomorrow.
u9-basketball-tomorrow.note: Begin with 我們, then the day, then 去 and the activity.

u9-soccer-like.note: Use 踢, kick, with 足球.

u9-soccer-suggest.note: Reuse the familiar suggestion ending 吧.

u9-soccer-fun.pinyin: Wǒ juéde tī zúqiú hěn hǎowán.
u9-soccer-fun.meaning: I think playing soccer is fun.
u9-soccer-fun.note: The opinion describes the entire activity 踢足球.

u9-tennis-or-swim.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng dǎ wǎngqiú háishì yóuyǒng?
u9-tennis-or-swim.meaning: Do you want to play tennis or swim?
u9-tennis-or-swim.note: Put 還是 between the alternatives; leave off 嗎.

u9-music-or-movies.text: 你喜歡聽音樂還是看電影？
u9-music-or-movies.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuān tīng yīnyuè háishì kàn diànyǐng?
u9-music-or-movies.meaning: Do you like listening to music or watching movies?
u9-music-or-movies.note: The shared 你喜歡 applies to both activities.

u9-basketball-or-soccer.text: 你喜歡打籃球還是踢足球？
u9-basketball-or-soccer.pinyin: Nǐ xǐhuān dǎ lánqiú háishì tī zúqiú?
u9-basketball-or-soccer.meaning: Do you like playing basketball or soccer?
u9-basketball-or-soccer.note: Keep 打籃球 and 踢足球 intact as the two alternatives.

u9-topic-tennis.meaning: As for playing tennis, I like it.
u9-topic-tennis.note: Start with 打網球 as the topic; the comment is 我喜歡.

u9-topic-music.meaning: As for listening to music, I like it a lot.
u9-topic-music.note: Start with the activity 聽音樂.

u9-both-sports.text: 打籃球、踢足球，我都喜歡。
u9-both-sports.pinyin: Dǎ lánqiú, tī zúqiú, wǒ dōu xǐhuān.
u9-both-sports.meaning: As for playing basketball and soccer, I like both.
u9-both-sports.note: List basketball first, then soccer, followed by the comment 我都喜歡.

u9-review-together.meaning: We are going swimming together tomorrow.
u9-review-together.note: Begin with 我們; place the day before 一起 and 去.
